boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain St Olaf College
boards.description: Ten currently documented food and convenience destinations with evening or late-night availability in Northfield and on the St. Olaf campus.

cards.title: The Lion’s Pause
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons, St. Olaf College
cards.notes: Use the Commons snack counter for an on-campus evening option; confirm the day’s service before heading over, especially during academic breaks.
cards.short_summary: Campus snacks and pizza delivery are listed through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists The Lion’s Pause for snacks and late-night options daily from 4 p.m. to midnight, with pizza delivery from 5 p.m. to midnight.
cards.access_notes: Official dining page lists daily hours of 4 p.m.–midnight; pizza delivery is listed 5 p.m.–midnight.

cards.title: The Cave
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons, St. Olaf College
cards.notes: Stop by the self-checkout convenience store for packaged food or essentials; use the posted schedule because weekend closing time changes.
cards.short_summary: A campus convenience store that stays open as late as 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf describes The Cave as a self-checkout convenience store open until midnight Sunday–Thursday and until 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: Sun–Thu 7 a.m.–midnight; Fri–Sat 7 a.m.–1 a.m.

cards.title: Carbone’s Pizza Northfield
cards.subtitle: 620 South Water Street, Northfield
cards.notes: Choose delivery, takeout, or dine-in and check the location page before ordering; it lists the latest closing window among these options.
cards.short_summary: Pizza, pasta, sandwiches, and salads with late posted hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Carbone’s official Northfield location page lists hours until 1 a.m. Monday–Saturday and until midnight Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official location hours: Mon–Sat 11 a.m.–1 a.m.; Sun 10 a.m.–midnight. Delivery and takeout are listed.

cards.title: Taco Bell on South Highway 3
cards.subtitle: 410 South Highway 3, Northfield
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru or delivery option when campus dining has closed; confirm operating status in the restaurant locator before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A Northfield drive-thru with 1 a.m. hours listed every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official Northfield page lists drive-thru hours from 7 a.m. to 1 a.m. daily and identifies the location as open late.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours of 7 a.m.–1 a.m. daily; dine-in is listed through 10 p.m. on the displayed schedule.

cards.title: Culver’s on Highway 3
cards.subtitle: 960 Highway 3 South, Northfield
cards.notes: Plan for dine-in or drive-thru service and check which lane is operating; the published drive-thru schedule extends later on midweek evenings.
cards.short_summary: Drive-thru service is listed until 11 p.m. Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Culver’s official Northfield page lists daily lobby hours until 10 p.m. and drive-thru hours until 11 p.m. Wednesday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Culver’s of Northfield, MN – Hwy 3 S
cards.access_notes: Official page: lobby daily 10 a.m.–10 p.m.; drive-thru Sun–Tue until 10 p.m. and Wed–Sat until 11 p.m.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on Clinton Lane
cards.subtitle: 1500 Clinton Lane, Suite 100, Northfield
cards.notes: Use the location’s carryout or delivery ordering page for a later Friday or Saturday food run; verify the order channel before placing it.
cards.short_summary: Friday and Saturday delivery and carryout are listed until 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut’s official Northfield location page lists delivery and carryout hours until 10 p.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists delivery and carryout until 10 p.m. Friday–Saturday and until 9 p.m. other days.

cards.title: Casey’s on Woodley Street
cards.subtitle: 521 Woodley Street West, Northfield
cards.notes: Use the store’s pickup or delivery ordering tools for evening snacks, pizza, sandwiches, or wings; allow time before the listed pickup cutoff.
cards.short_summary: Convenience-store food pickup and delivery are listed until 9:30 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Casey’s official store page lists its Northfield Woodley Street location open until 10 p.m., with pickup and delivery available until 9:30 p.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists store hours 5 a.m.–10 p.m. and pickup/delivery 5 a.m.–9:30 p.m. daily.

cards.title: Rosemary Italian Kitchen
cards.subtitle: 2300 Gleason Court, Northfield
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s order or reservation options for an evening meal; the official site posts the same nightly closing time across the week.
cards.short_summary: An Italian restaurant with hours listed through 9 p.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Rosemary Italian Kitchen’s official website lists the Northfield restaurant’s hours as 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Monday–Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Monday–Sunday hours of 11 a.m.–9 p.m.

cards.title: Stav Hall
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons, St. Olaf College
cards.notes: Use continuous weekday dining before late evening plans; review the menu and current service schedule, since limited offerings appear between main meals.
cards.short_summary: Campus dining is listed continuously through 8 p.m. on weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists Stav Hall as open Monday–Friday from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., with limited options between standard meal periods.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists weekday continuous dining 7 a.m.–8 p.m.; dinner service is listed until 8 p.m. Monday–Thursday.

cards.title: The Cage
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons, St. Olaf College
cards.notes: Use the Get App for pickup from the made-to-order counter and check the weekend schedule before going, as opening times differ from weekdays.
cards.short_summary: A made-to-order campus option listed until 8 p.m. every day.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s dining page lists The Cage made-to-order menu available until 8 p.m. Monday–Friday and Saturday–Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists The Cage until 8 p.m. daily: 7:30 a.m. weekday start and 9 a.m. weekend start.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named spaces within St. Olaf’s student-centered Buntrock Commons, documented by the college as places for students to study, meet, socialize, and gather.

cards.title: Buntrock Commons
cards.subtitle: Student-centered commons on the Hill
cards.notes: Start here to orient a campus day: the Commons brings student services, dining, gathering areas, and building support into one shared destination.
cards.short_summary: The campus commons that connects daily student services and shared spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf describes Buntrock Commons as the physical and social crossroads of campus life and a student-centered Commons.
cards.access_notes: Visitors and guests are welcomed but must follow college and building policies.

cards.title: Fireside Lounge
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons student space
cards.notes: Use this named lounge as a meetup point before a study session or conversation, and leave it open for others when you finish.
cards.short_summary: A named lounge in the Commons’ student-space lineup.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists Fireside Lounge among Buntrock Commons student spaces and says these spaces support students studying, meeting, and socializing.
cards.access_notes: The college says most student spaces are intentionally not reservable so they remain accessible for Oles.

cards.title: The Cage
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons made-to-order dining
cards.notes: Plan a casual food or coffee stop between commitments; check the dining page for the current menu and schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A made-to-order dining counter in Buntrock Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf identifies The Cage as a Buntrock Commons dining option with a made-to-order menu.
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours: Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–8 p.m.; Saturday–Sunday 9 a.m.–8 p.m.

cards.title: The Lion’s Pause
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons late-night dining and event space
cards.notes: Meet over a snack or use the venue as an evening activity stop; confirm its current menu and event details through campus dining.
cards.short_summary: A named Commons venue for snacks, late-night food, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists The Lion’s Pause as a Buntrock student space and as a dining location for snacks and late-night options.
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours are every day, 4 p.m.–midnight; pizza delivery is posted for 5 p.m.–midnight.

cards.title: Buntrock Plaza
cards.subtitle: Outdoor community space at Buntrock Commons
cards.notes: Use the plaza as a recognizable outdoor rendezvous point, then move inside or onward once your group is together.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor gathering space at the Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists Buntrock Plaza among Buntrock Commons’ community spaces for gathering, conversation, and celebration.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted Commons policies; visitor parking is in the lot directly across from the north entrance.

cards.title: Crossroads
cards.subtitle: Ground-floor Buntrock Commons gathering area
cards.notes: Choose Crossroads for a central meeting point or to get building directions from the nearby Information Desk before exploring campus.
cards.short_summary: A named Commons gathering area with nearby wayfinding help.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists Crossroads as a Buntrock Commons community space, and locates the Information Desk there on the ground floor.
cards.access_notes: The Information Desk is staffed during building hours and can help with directions, dining hours, and technical support.

cards.title: Viking Theater
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons community space
cards.notes: Check campus programming for a scheduled use, or use this named venue as a clear landmark when coordinating with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A named theater space within the Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists Viking Theater among Buntrock Commons’ community spaces.
cards.access_notes: Event or room access may depend on scheduling; consult Buntrock Commons for current availability.

cards.title: Norway Room
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons meeting space
cards.notes: For a planned group session, identify the Norway Room by name and coordinate through the Commons’ meeting-space process when a reservation is needed.
cards.short_summary: A named meeting room in Buntrock Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists the Norway Room among Buntrock Commons meeting spaces, which are available for student organizations, study sessions, and collaborations.
cards.access_notes: Meeting-space availability and reservations are managed through Buntrock Commons processes.

cards.title: Trollhaugen
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons meeting space
cards.notes: Use Trollhaugen’s exact room name when planning a student-organization meeting, academic work session, or cross-campus collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A named Commons meeting room for organized group work.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists Trollhaugen among Buntrock Commons meeting spaces for student organizations, study sessions, and cross-campus collaborations.
cards.access_notes: Confirm room availability and reservation requirements with Buntrock Commons before making plans.

cards.title: Valhalla
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons meeting space
cards.notes: Use Valhalla’s exact room name when organizing a collaborative session, and leave setup or access details to the Commons reservation process.
cards.short_summary: A named meeting room within the student-centered Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf lists Valhalla among Buntrock Commons meeting spaces for student organizations, study sessions, and cross-campus collaborations.
cards.access_notes: Confirm room availability and reservation requirements with Buntrock Commons before making plans.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten free, daylight-friendly outdoor meet-ups in St. Olaf’s Natural Lands.

cards.title: Walk Big Pond Loop
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Meet at the Big Pond trailhead, take the loop at an easy pace, and pause to notice the prairie and wetland views together.
cards.short_summary: A short named loop for a no-cost outdoor catch-up.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Big Pond Loop, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; remain on marked trails and follow posted notices.

cards.title: Take the Baseball Pond Loop
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Use this named loop for a walking conversation, then head back before dark; bring water and leave plants and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A free trail loop beside a named Natural Lands pond.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Baseball Pond Loop, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; stay on designated routes and observe trail conditions.

cards.title: Climb Norway Valley Trail
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Choose this wooded trail for a brief daylight reset with friends; its narrow, uneven route calls for sturdy shoes and a slower pace.
cards.short_summary: A free wooded walk through a named Natural Lands area.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Norway Valley Trail, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; the college describes Norway Valley as narrow and steep in places.

cards.title: Walk Heath Creek Trail
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Plan a daylight walk with a friend along this named trail, keeping to the route and giving yourself extra time after rain or snow.
cards.short_summary: A free trail hang in the Heath Creek section of the Natural Lands.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Heath Creek Trail, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; use marked trails and comply with any seasonal restrictions.

cards.title: Head Out on Windmill Trail
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Use the trail for a quick shared walk and a view of the wind turbine; stay together, follow the marked route, and pack out trash.
cards.short_summary: A free named trail with a campus wind-turbine landmark nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Windmill Trail, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; use designated paths and follow posted safety guidance.

cards.title: Stroll Ellingson Woods Trail
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Set a relaxed walking pace through this named woods trail, then compare what you notice on the way back without leaving the path.
cards.short_summary: A free woodland walk for a quiet two-person or small-group hang.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Ellingson Woods Trail, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; stay on trail and check weather before going.

cards.title: Circle the Prairie Loop
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Meet for a loop through open prairie, bring sun protection when needed, and use the walk as a phone-free conversation break.
cards.short_summary: A free named prairie route for an easy outdoor reset.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Prairie Loop, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; remain on marked trails and prepare for exposed conditions.

cards.title: Walk Forest Restoration Loop 1
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a slow loop through the restoration area, using the trail map to stay oriented and leaving natural materials in place.
cards.short_summary: A free named loop through St. Olaf’s restored natural landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Forest Restoration Loop 1, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; respect restoration areas and posted directions.

cards.title: Explore Forest Restoration Loop 2
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Pick this shorter named loop for a between-classes walk, taking photos from the trail and keeping the group on the established route.
cards.short_summary: A free, map-listed forest loop for a quick shared break.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies Forest Restoration Loop 2, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; check the current trail map and weather before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the STOGROW Trail
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands trail
cards.notes: Take a short walk on the named trail with friends, pausing to observe the adjacent landscape without entering work or growing areas.
cards.short_summary: A free, map-listed trail near St. Olaf’s sustainability landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Natural Lands map identifies STOGROW Trail, and the City of Northfield states that the public has free access to trails in the natural areas around St. Olaf.
cards.access_notes: The Natural Lands are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; remain on the trail and respect active farm or restoration operations.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented St. Olaf study environments, spanning quiet reading rooms, collaborative technology spaces, libraries, and available classrooms.

cards.title: Reference Room
cards.subtitle: Rolvaag Memorial Library
cards.notes: Enter through Rolvaag’s main doors, use the last door on the right, then veer left for the silent, window-lit room.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent-study room with prominent windows and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf identifies the Reference Room as a silent study space in Rolvaag Memorial Library with stunning windows and a light-filled setting.
cards.access_notes: Located in Rolvaag Memorial Library; follow the official route from the main entrance.

cards.title: DiSCO
cards.subtitle: Rolvaag Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring a project or group task and use the technology-focused study and meeting space; reserve DiSCO spaces for organized use.
cards.short_summary: A library-based study and meeting space with academic technology resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The DiSCO is a study and meeting space in Rolvaag Memorial Library with resources supporting academic technology use; its spaces are reservable.
cards.access_notes: DiSCO spaces are reservable for courses, events, and student-organization activities.

cards.title: Ole’s Cave
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor, Rolvaag Memorial Library
cards.notes: Settle in with a reading-heavy assignment and use the sofas or armchairs; plan around the room’s limited table space.
cards.short_summary: A secluded fourth-floor reading room furnished with plush seating.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Academic Support guide describes Ole’s Cave as a fourth-floor Rolvaag room with plush sofas and armchairs, suited to extended reading.
cards.source_title: Places to Study at St. Olaf
cards.access_notes: The guide notes limited table space and that the room also contains DVDs.

cards.title: Rolvaag’s First-Floor Study Pits
cards.subtitle: First floor, Rolvaag Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring your materials to the cushioned study pits for a focused session; choose this floor when you need a quiet setting.
cards.short_summary: A quiet Rolvaag floor with cushioned bench-style study pits.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Academic Support guide identifies the first floor of Rolvaag as a quiet study floor with cushioned study pits.
cards.source_title: Places to Study at St. Olaf
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 1 of Rolvaag; check the library’s current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Science Library
cards.subtitle: Regents Hall of Natural Science
cards.notes: Use the hillside-facing windows for a naturally lit reading or problem-set session in Regents Hall’s library setting.
cards.short_summary: A focused library environment with large windows overlooking the hillside.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Academic Support guide places the Science Library in Regents Hall and notes its large windows overlooking the hillside.
cards.source_title: Places to Study at St. Olaf
cards.access_notes: Located in Regents Hall; confirm building access and room availability on arrival.

cards.title: Tomson Hall Classrooms
cards.subtitle: Tomson Hall
cards.notes: Check the room schedule first, then use an unreserved classroom’s wall-sized writable surface to map out a problem or draft.
cards.short_summary: Available classrooms with paint-covered walls that function as oversized whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Academic Support guide says unoccupied Tomson Hall classrooms can be used for work and have walls that function as giant whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Places to Study at St. Olaf
cards.access_notes: Use only when no class or reservation occupies the room; Public Safety lists Tomson’s regular building-hours schedule.

cards.title: Holland Hall Classrooms
cards.subtitle: Holland Hall
cards.notes: Find an unreserved classroom and use the chalkboard or blackboard for equations, diagrams, outlines, or group review.
cards.short_summary: Available classrooms equipped with chalkboards and blackboards.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s Academic Support guide says empty Holland Hall classrooms can be used as study rooms and include chalk and blackboards.
cards.source_title: Places to Study at St. Olaf
cards.access_notes: Use only when the classroom is not reserved or in scheduled use.

cards.title: Boe Undercroft
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Boe Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Head to the chapel’s lower level with a laptop or reading; use the relaxed gathering area for a change of scenery.
cards.short_summary: A relaxed student gathering space beneath Boe Memorial Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf identifies the Boe Undercroft, beneath Boe Memorial Chapel, as a relaxed gathering space for students.
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level of Boe Memorial Chapel.

cards.title: Halvorson Music Library
cards.subtitle: Main floor, Christiansen Hall of Music
cards.notes: Use the individual or group listening and viewing facilities when your coursework involves scores, recordings, or music research.
cards.short_summary: A music library with individual and group listening and viewing facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Halvorson Music Library is on Christiansen Hall’s main floor and provides individual and group viewing/listening facilities plus an electronic piano with headphones.
cards.source_title: Halvorson Music Library – St. Olaf Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on the main floor of Christiansen Hall of Music; library hours are posted by St. Olaf Libraries.

cards.title: Hong Kierkegaard Library
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf College campus
cards.notes: Use an open cubicle for philosophy research and return books to the designated area; library materials remain inside the library.
cards.short_summary: A special-collections research library with first-come, first-served cubicle space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hong Kierkegaard Library offers open, first-come-first-served cubicle space and requires its special-collections resources to remain inside the library.
cards.source_title: The Collection – The Hong Kierkegaard Library
cards.access_notes: Cubicles cannot be reserved in summer; use open seats or unused spaces, and keep library resources in the building.

warnings: Some study-location details come from St. Olaf’s currently hosted Academic Support PDF; confirm room access and availability before visiting.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: A self-guided look at ten named stops on or immediately beside Division Street, Northfield’s historic downtown corridor.

cards.title: Nutting Block
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 220 Division St
cards.notes: Pause at 220 Division to study the 1893 Richardsonian Romanesque façade, then use the History Center’s Digital Division page for its building story.
cards.short_summary: A 1893 downtown building with a long retail-and-office history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nutting Block was constructed in 1893 in the Richardsonian Romanesque style and later became the Nutting Mall.
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

cards.title: Old City Hall
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 302 Division St
cards.notes: Look for the large street-level opening that recalls the former fire-station bay, then read the Digital Division account of the 1876 civic building.
cards.short_summary: A former City Hall and fire station with visible architectural traces.
cards.evidence_claim: Built in 1876, Old City Hall housed Northfield civic functions and a fire station; the original fire-wagon arches were later replaced by one large opening.
cards.source_title: Old City Hall — Northfield History Center
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

cards.title: Northfield News Building
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 311–313 Division St
cards.notes: Stand across Division Street to take in the upper façade, then follow the Digital Division story of the 1964 fire and the building’s survival.
cards.short_summary: The former newspaper headquarters retains its historic upper façade.
cards.evidence_claim: The Northfield News Building dates to 1884; after a 1964 fire collapsed its roof, its exterior walls remained standing and the upper façade survives.
cards.source_title: Northfield News Building — Northfield History Center
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

cards.title: French Building
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 317 Division St
cards.notes: Find the 317 Division address and compare it with neighboring façades; the Digital Division page identifies this as the 300 block’s oldest building.
cards.short_summary: The oldest building on Division Street’s 300 block.
cards.evidence_claim: The French Building at 317 Division Street was built in 1872 and is the oldest building on the historic district’s 300 block.
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

cards.title: First Mergen Building
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 321 Division St
cards.notes: Use the 321 Division address as a waypoint and read the Digital Division entry to trace the first of the three Mergen estate buildings.
cards.short_summary: The first surviving Division Street building associated with the Mergen estate.
cards.evidence_claim: The First Mergen Building was built in 1882 by Barney Mergen and was the first of three Mergen estate buildings on Division Street.
cards.source_title: First Mergen Building — Northfield History Center
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

cards.title: Central Block
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 401–405 Division St
cards.notes: Look up to the northwest-corner tower and its cone roof, then open the Digital Division page for architectural details and the 1893 construction story.
cards.short_summary: A Queen Anne-style commercial block marked by a corner tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Central Block at 401–405 Division Street was built in 1893 and is distinguished by a cone-roofed northwest-corner tower and Queen Anne details.
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

cards.title: Scriver Building
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 408 Division St
cards.notes: Stop at 408 Division and use the Northfield History Center’s nearby museum and Digital Division materials to place the building in the downtown story.
cards.short_summary: A named historic building in the core of Division Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Northfield History Center identifies the Scriver Building at 408 Division Street as a stop on its Digital Division tour of historic downtown buildings.
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. The nearby museum has separate admission and operating information.

cards.title: Lockwood Opera House
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 419–421 Division St
cards.notes: At 419–421 Division, imagine the upstairs performance space and read the Digital Division entry about the opera house’s role in local entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A former 19th-century performance venue on Division Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lockwood Opera House was built in 1872 and opened for business in 1873, becoming an early Northfield entertainment venue.
cards.source_title: Lockwood Opera House — Northfield History Center
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

cards.title: Scofield Building
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 501 Division St
cards.notes: Walk to the Division and East Fifth corner, then consult the Digital Division entry for the rebuilt 1868 structure and its long commercial history.
cards.short_summary: One of the oldest surviving buildings in historic downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Scofield Building at 501 Division Street was built in 1868 and was almost entirely rebuilt after an 1878 fire.
cards.access_notes: At the Division Street and East Fifth Street intersection; view the exterior from public sidewalks.

cards.title: Olson Building
cards.subtitle: Division Street corridor — 504 Division St
cards.notes: Find 504 Division and use the Digital Division page to follow how this 1890 building helped establish the 500 block as part of downtown.
cards.short_summary: A 500-block building tied to the late-1800s growth of Division Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Olson Building at 504 Division Street was constructed in 1890; the History Center describes it as part of the 500 block’s late-19th-century development.
cards.access_notes: On Division Street; view the exterior from public sidewalks. Individual tenants set their own access conditions.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented St. Olaf traditions, annual events, and recurring Hill practices.

cards.title: St. Olaf Christmas Festival
cards.subtitle: Annual music tradition in Boe Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Check the current festival schedule and ticket information before planning a visit; the event brings St. Olaf ensembles together for holiday performances.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus Christmas celebration built around St. Olaf’s choirs and orchestra.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf identifies its Christmas Festival as an annual tradition that brings five choirs and the St. Olaf Orchestra together.
cards.access_notes: Attendance arrangements vary by festival year; consult the official festival information.

cards.title: St. Olaf Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual campus and alumni gathering
cards.notes: Use the college’s current Homecoming information for event details, then choose an official program activity that fits your visit and access needs.
cards.short_summary: A recurring St. Olaf gathering that includes the football game and alumni programming.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s traditions page describes Homecoming week with the football game as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Programs, venues, and attendance requirements vary annually.

cards.title: Champion of the Hill
cards.subtitle: Annual Homecoming competition
cards.notes: Look for the current Homecoming schedule and follow organizer instructions if the competition is open to your group; it is listed as an annual tradition.
cards.short_summary: A named annual competition associated with St. Olaf Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s traditions page identifies the annual King of the Hill competition, pictured there as Champion of the Hill, as part of Homecoming.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current event name, format, and participant eligibility through Homecoming organizers.

cards.title: Hawaiian Night
cards.subtitle: Recurring Stav Hall dining-hall event
cards.notes: Watch St. Olaf dining announcements for the current date and entry rules; attend through normal dining access and respect dining-hall guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named St. Olaf dining tradition held in Stav Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s traditions page names Hawaiian Night in Stav Dining Hall as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Availability and dining access are determined by the college for each occurrence.

cards.title: Outdoor Opera
cards.subtitle: Annual spring outdoor performance
cards.notes: Check Music Department and campus-event listings for the current production, location, weather plan, and attendance arrangements before traveling to campus.
cards.short_summary: An annual spring opera performance staged outdoors at St. Olaf.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s traditions page identifies an annual outdoor opera each spring as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Production timing, site, and attendance arrangements vary by year.

cards.title: Intramural Broomball
cards.subtitle: January campus recreation competition
cards.notes: Review the current Recreation or intramural registration information before joining; follow organizer safety and equipment requirements for the scheduled competition.
cards.short_summary: A recurring January intramural competition named among St. Olaf traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s traditions page identifies intramural broomball competition each January as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Registration, rules, and participant eligibility are set for the current intramural season.

cards.title: International Night
cards.subtitle: Student-organized annual cultural showcase
cards.notes: Check the current International Night announcement for performance and audience details; the event invites students to share culture through organized programming.
cards.short_summary: An annual student-organized showcase of music, dance, and spoken word.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf calls International Night an annual college tradition and describes it as a student-organized event where students share pieces of their cultures.
cards.source_title: Student-organized International Night an annual St. Olaf tradition
cards.access_notes: Scheduling, venue, and audience access are announced for the current year.

cards.title: Multilingual Caroling
cards.subtitle: December caroling in Latin, Greek, and German
cards.notes: Look for December communications from participating academic departments and join only through the organized route; the tradition visits several named campus spaces.
cards.short_summary: A December St. Olaf caroling practice performed in three languages.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf reports that students have gathered each December for more than four decades to sing Christmas carols in Latin, Greek, and German.
cards.source_title: St. Olaf students spread holiday cheer with multilingual caroling tradition
cards.access_notes: Participation and route details depend on the organizers’ current plans.

cards.title: Um! Yah! Yah!
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf’s century-old fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the song at an official campus event and follow event leaders’ cues; the college archive documents its long connection to St. Olaf life.
cards.short_summary: The school fight song that has been associated with St. Olaf events for more than a century.
cards.evidence_claim: A St. Olaf Magazine history states that “Um! Yah! Yah!” has been a staple at St. Olaf events for more than 100 years.
cards.source_title: Bound by Song: Um! Yah! Yah! | St. Olaf Magazine
cards.access_notes: See the official college history for the song’s background and campus use.

cards.title: Daily Chapel
cards.subtitle: Recurring worship in Boe Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Review the live chapel schedule before attending and follow the service’s posted guidance; special events and academic-calendar changes can affect programming.
cards.short_summary: Regular chapel worship is listed among the college’s continuing traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s traditions page identifies daily chapel and special events in Boe Chapel as part of campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Check the current chapel calendar for service times and visitor information.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at St Olaf College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented on the Hill, finding a few campus anchors, and taking a daylight walk through the Natural Lands.

cards.title: Begin at the Information Desk
cards.subtitle: Crossroads, Buntrock Commons
cards.notes: Ask for directions, current dining information, transportation schedules, or technical-support guidance before setting out around campus.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for campus wayfinding and current services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Information Desk is on Buntrock Commons’ ground-floor Crossroads and provides directions, dining hours, transportation schedules, and technical-support information.
cards.access_notes: The college says the desk is staffed during Buntrock building hours; confirm hours on arrival.

cards.title: Settle into Fireside Lounge
cards.subtitle: Buntrock Commons
cards.notes: Use this named student space for a short reset, a conversation, or to review the day’s campus plans with your group.
cards.short_summary: A documented student space inside the campus commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Buntrock Commons identifies Fireside Lounge among its student spaces and says most such spaces are intentionally unreservable to remain accessible for Oles.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to building access and any posted space rules.

cards.title: Find a calm corner in Rolvaag
cards.subtitle: East side of campus, connected to Buntrock Commons
cards.notes: Walk through the library’s levels, locate its study areas, and save the service desk location for a future research question.
cards.short_summary: A campus library stop with study space and collections across multiple levels.
cards.evidence_claim: Rolvaag Memorial Library is connected to Buntrock Commons and has collections and services distributed across five and a half levels.
cards.source_title: Rolvaag Memorial Library – St. Olaf Libraries
cards.access_notes: Library hours are maintained on the library page; check them before visiting.

cards.title: See what is on view at Flaten
cards.subtitle: Main Floor, Center for Art and Dance
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition page, then make time for a gallery visit when the museum is open during your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art museum in the Center for Art and Dance.
cards.evidence_claim: Flaten Art Museum is on the Main Floor of the Center for Art and Dance, and its official visitor page states that admission is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit – Flaten Art Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum’s official page says galleries are closed for summer break and reopen September 11, 2026; verify current hours before going.

cards.title: Pause by Boe Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf campus
cards.notes: Add the chapel to your campus walk and consult the college calendar for public concerts, recitals, or other scheduled programs.
cards.short_summary: A prominent campus performance and gathering venue.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf’s music site states that organ lessons are typically held in Boe Chapel on its Holtkamp Organ.
cards.access_notes: Interior access and events vary; follow posted access guidance and the college calendar.

cards.title: Spot the St. Olaf Rock
cards.subtitle: Outside Tomson Hall
cards.notes: Find the carved granite boulder outside Tomson Hall and take a quick look at a physical piece of the college’s documented history.
cards.short_summary: A named historic campus landmark near Tomson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The St. Olaf Archives identifies the St. Olaf Rock as a granite boulder outside Tomson Hall and documents its carved early representation of the college seal.
cards.source_title: Tidbits: Discovering St. Olaf: The St. Olaf Rock – College Archives
cards.access_notes: View from exterior campus walkways and respect any nearby building-access rules.

cards.title: Walk Norway Valley in daylight
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands
cards.notes: Choose a marked daylight route, stay on the trail, and take a slower look at this wooded section of the Natural Lands.
cards.short_summary: The campus’s oldest forest area, with documented native hardwoods.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf identifies Norway Valley as a 15-acre parcel of native hardwood trees and the oldest forest area on campus.
cards.source_title: Habitats and Management of the Natural Lands
cards.access_notes: Remain on trails and follow Natural Lands rules; visit in daylight and with appropriate footwear.

cards.title: Take the Big Pond Loop
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands
cards.notes: Download or pick up the Natural Lands map, then use the suggested Big Pond Loop as a self-guided outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A mapped Natural Lands route with a college-published suggested walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The Natural Lands wellness-walks page lists Big Pond Loop among its suggested walking routes, and the trail-map page provides downloadable maps.
cards.access_notes: Use the current trail map and follow Natural Lands safety and trail-use rules.

cards.title: Find Big Ole by the Art Barn
cards.subtitle: St. Olaf Natural Lands
cards.notes: Use the wind turbine as a visual landmark on a daylight Natural Lands walk, then continue only on mapped, permitted routes.
cards.short_summary: A named campus wind turbine beside the Natural Lands.
cards.evidence_claim: A St. Olaf page identifies the campus wind turbine as “BIG OLE” and states that the HORIZON sculpture was installed next to it in February 2023.
cards.source_title: Presenters – 2024 – Conference on Worship, Theology, and the Arts
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an outdoor landmark; do not enter restricted utility or maintenance areas.

cards.title: End with a mapped nature walk
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to St. Olaf College
cards.notes: Finish the weekend with a route matched to your daylight, weather, and footwear; keep to trails and leave plants and wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: More than 430 adjacent acres for documented recreation, conservation, and education.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Olaf says the Natural Lands encompass approximately 430 acres adjacent to campus and welcomes visitors to explore while following its safety and environmental rules.
cards.access_notes: The college asks visitors to follow Natural Lands rules; trails are open for outdoor use, with restrictions including no camping or fires.
